title: An Italian Eight String Mandoline labelled IL GLOBO, Naples, circa 1900. The pear-shaped back of rosewood, the soundhole and surround ornamented with patterned mother-o'-pearl, with a case, and a Mandoline by F. DE MUREDA, Naples, labelled and dated 1906. The latter as seen (2)

A Violin of the NEUNER School, circa 1830. Length of back 14 1/4in. (362mm.). The two-piece back of narrow figure, the ribs of varied figure, the scroll plain, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a red-brown colour

Condition fair

A Violin attributed to J. FRANCOIS BRETON, Mirecourt, circa 1770, labelled in manuscript, SILVESTRE repaired by H. COLE, Liverpool. Length of back 14 5/16in. (363mm.), with two bows in a case by W. A Good Violin by MICHEL COUTURIEUX bearing the maker's label in Paris, dated 1888, and signed in the peg box. Length of back 14 3/16in. (360mm.), with a bow in case. An Interesting Violin, circa 1770, labelled MARIO CERUTI, Milan, 1914. Length of back 13 15/16in. (354mm.), in case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs of medium curl, the peg box plain, the volute odd, the table of medium grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of a golden-brown colour with some addition. The model after GRAGNANI

A Good French Violin, circa 1890 of the Colin School and labelled Lutherie Artistique, CLAUDE LEBLANC. Length of back 14 1/8in. (359mm.), with a bow in case. A Violin of the KLOZ, Mittenwald School, circa 1740, and labelled JOSEPH GAGLIANO. Length of back 13 15/16in. (355mm.), in case. The two-piece back of faint medium figure, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium open grain, the varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground

A French Violin, circa 1770, by a member of the CHAPPUY family, bearing a brand below the button A. CHUPPUY. Length of back 14 1/16in. (357mm.), with a bow in case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of an opaque deep brown colour on the original varnish.  There appears to have been at least two members of the CHAPPUY family—the manner of work being at variance

A German Violin, circa 1740, bearing the label MATHIAS ALBANI, Bolsani, Anno 1684. Length of back 14in. (356mm.), in a shaped case by Edward Withers, London. An English Violin, circa 1780 of the BETTS School. Length of back 13 15/16in. (354mm.). The two-piece back cut on the slab showing faint medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain widening slightly to the flanks, the varnish of a thin red-brown colour

An English Violin, circa 1790. Length of back 13 15/16in. (355mm.), in mahogany veneer case. The one-piece back of narrow curl, the ribs and scroll of similar figure, the table of broad wavy grain, the varnish of a clear brown colour. The model after the Testore School. Original neck and bassbar

A Violin of the MARTIN WIDHALM SCHOOL, Nurnberg, circa 1770. Length of back 14in. (356mm.), in case. The two-piece back of faint figure, the ribs of narrow curl, the scroll plain, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of an opaque red colour on a brown ground

A Violin by CARLO GUILANI bearing the maker's manuscript label in Innsbruck, dated 1910. Length of back 14 3/8in. (365mm.), in a shaped wood case. The two-piece back, ribs and scroll of medium flame, the table of narrow grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of an orange-red colour

A Violin, circa 1780. Length of back 13 7/8in. (354mm.). The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of close grain widening to medium grain on the flanks, the varnish of a golden-orange-brown colour. The inlaid purfling of broad diamond pattern.  With a certificate of MESSRS. JOHN DYKE, Malvern, dated 1971. That it is an example of Neapolitan work, circa 1760-1770

A French Violin, made in the workshops of NESTOR AUDINOT, bearing a label N. AUDINOT, 17 Boulevard Bonne-Nouvelle, Annee 1898, No. 676, and branded on the inner back. Length of back 14 3/16in (360mm.), with a bow stamped N. AUDINOT À PARIS, in an oblong double Violin case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of strong medium grain, the varnish of an orange colour on a yellow ground. The model after GUARNERI

The handsome two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain widening to the flanks, the transparent varnish of an orange-brown colour

Painted purfling. Excellent condition

A Bohemian Viola, circa 1930. Length of back 16 1/8in. (410mm.), with a bow in a shaped, plush lined case with waterproof cover.
